## The Framingham Heart Study <img src="map.png" height="120px" style="vertical-align:middle;"> 
*  *Long-term*, **Multigenerational**, study conducted in *Framingham Massachusetts* from 1948- 

::: {.info-box}
 <ul >
    <li class="fragment"><i class="fa-solid fa-bullseye"></i>The study aimed to help identify common factors in Cardiovascular Disease</li>
    <li class="fragment"><i class="fa-solid fa-bowl-food"></i>Primary outcome: incident coronary heart disease (CHD), defined as first-onset CHD events during follow-up.</li>
    <li class="fragment"><i class="fa-solid fa-link"></i>Details can be found [here](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(13)61752-3/fulltext).</li>
</ul>
:::


## The Dataset

*  The dataset was accessed from [kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aasheesh200/framingham-heart-study-dataset)

::: {.info-box}
<ul>
  <li class="fragment"><i class="fa-solid fa-table"></i> Dimensions: <strong>4,240 rows</strong> and <strong>16 variables</strong>.</li>
  <li class="fragment"><i class="fa-solid fa-triangle-exclamation"></i> Missingness proportions were highest for: <strong>Glucose (9.15%)</strong>, <strong>Education (2.48%)</strong>, <strong>Blood Pressure(1.25%)</strong>, and <strong>Total Cholesterol (1.18%)</strong>.</li>
  <li class="fragment"><i class="fa-solid fa-magnifying-glass-chart"></i> Other predictors with missingness: <strong>Cigarettes/Day (0.68%)</strong>, <strong>BMI (0.45%)</strong>, and <strong>Heart Rate (0.02%)</strong>.</li>
</ul>
:::

- This missingness pattern motivates using **MICE** to retain observations and reduce bias from complete-case analysis. <img src="missing_pattern.png" style="height:90px; vertical-align:middle; margin-left:10px;">

## MICE <img src="MICE.png" style="height:80px; vertical-align:middle; position:relative; "> <span class="mice-cite"><a href="https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v045i03">Van Buuren (2011)</a></span> {.mice-slide}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.mice-box}
<p class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1"><strong>Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE)</strong> fills missing values by iteratively modeling each incomplete variable using the others.</p>

<p class="fragment" data-fragment-index="3">Here we set variable-specific methods (<code>norm</code>, <code>logreg</code>, <code>polr</code>) and keep <code>TenYearCHD</code> as a predictor without imputing it.</p>

<p class="fragment" data-fragment-index="4">The algorithm cycles through incomplete variables until values stabilize.</p>

:::
:::

::: {.column .fragment width="58%" data-fragment-index="2"}
```{r des}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "|1-3|5-14|16-20|"
init <- mice(train_data, maxit = 0, print = FALSE)
meth <- init$method
pred <- init$predictorMatrix

meth[] <- ""
meth["cigsPerDay"] <- "norm"
meth["BPMeds"] <- "logreg"
meth["education"] <- "polr"
meth["totChol"] <- "norm"
meth["BMI"] <- "norm"
meth["heartRate"] <- "norm"
meth["glucose"] <- "norm"
meth["TenYearCHD"] <- ""
pred["TenYearCHD", ] <- 0

framing.imputed.train <- mice(
  data = train_data, m = 20, method = meth,
  predictorMatrix = pred, seed = 214, maxit = 5
)
train_complete <- complete(framing.imputed.train)
```

::: {.info-box .fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
<ul>
  <li><strong>Data split:</strong> 70% train, 30% test.</li>
  <li><strong>Why MICE:</strong> preserves sample size and reduces complete-case bias.</li>
</ul>
:::
:::
